reported_quantity: % of US adults who think a lot or some of the health information they see on social media is false or misleading
denominator: 4,741 US adults aged 18+ with complete data on all study variables (HINTS 7, 2024, two-stage address-based national sample)
misinfo_definition: “information that is false, inaccurate, or misleading according to the best available evidence at the time”

reported_quantity: % of Ebola prevention/cure tweets classified as medical misinformation
denominator: 564 English-language tweets containing 'Ebola' and 'prevention' or 'cure' sent from Guinea, Liberia and Nigeria, 1-7 September 2014
misinfo_definition: 'we grouped them into medically correct information, medical misinformation, and other (including tweets of a spiritual nature)'

reported_quantity: % of news source links shared in political and social-issue Twitter spaces that came from problematic sources
denominator: All news source links shared in the keyword/hashtag datasets for presidential candidates, parties and social issues; around a million links to media articles were shared across the three time frames (per-period count not stated)
misinfo_definition: Problematic sources refer to Jack's characterization as containing information that is "inaccurate, misleading, inappropriately attributed, or altogether fabricated" (2017, p. 1)

reported_quantity: % of respondents reporting self-assessed exposure to misinformation about Covid-19 on social media in the past month
denominator: 1,500 French respondents (Lightspeed Kantar online panel, quota-matched to census)
misinfo_definition: “The next questions will be about misinformation on social media. By misinformation, we mean false or misleading information.”

reported_quantity: % of Albanian journalists who say they encountered disinformation campaigns or bombardment with dubious information
denominator: 42 professional Albanian journalists who completed an online questionnaire, contacted through the main newsrooms
misinfo_definition: "dis-information as information that is false and intentionally created to harm a person, social group, organization, or state, while mis-information is indeed false information, but not created with the intent to cause harm" (Wardle & Derakhshan, 2017, as cited by the author)

reported_quantity: % of links posted on 4chan's /pol/ board coded as junk news (conspiracy, propaganda or sensationalist)
denominator: Links posted in US-flagged 4chan /pol/ posts to the 182 hostnames that appeared over 400 times and were manually coded (link count not stated)
misinfo_definition: 'junk' news, which Howard et al. define as content "extremist, sensationalist, conspiratorial, masked commentary, [or] fake" that presents itself as news

reported_quantity: % of Information Sciences students who reported having shared disinformation (deliberately false information)
denominator: 51 Information Sciences students at the Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences, Osijek (of 109 valid responses); denominator includes 5 'cannot determine' answers
misinfo_definition: "Disinformation, on the other hand, is also false information, but it is deliberately spread with the knowledge that it is untrue."

reported_quantity: % of English-language YouTube videos about external cephalic version scored 'not useful' (<9 of 30 points) on a composite usefulness instrument
denominator: 70 YouTube videos remaining after duplicates and exclusions from the first 35 relevance-sorted results for each of five ECV search terms (175 selected)
misinfo_definition: "Points could be deducted from the total usefulness score if either proven or unproven misinformation was given about the procedure, risks, pain, success rate, or the chance of the baby turning back in breech position."

reported_quantity: % of respondents who self-reported recalling seeing prominent false claims about the virus's origins / the nature of the government's response, averaged across headlines in that category
denominator: 1,045 U.S. adults surveyed via Qualtrics, recruited on Lucid with quota sampling matched to the U.S. population on age, gender, ethnicity and region
misinfo_definition: "misinformation headlines that had circulated widely on social media", identified by searching news coverage in major U.S. newspapers and prominent fact-checking websites

reported_quantity: % of chatbot answers to ten ACL (sports medicine) questions judged by expert surgeons to contain misinformation
denominator: 20 chatbot answers (the first ten non-duplicate 'people also ask' questions from a Google search on 'anterior cruciate ligament', put to ChatGPT-3.5 and to Google Bard)
misinfo_definition: "Misinformation spread was defined as the dissemination of erroneous, misleading or false information."

reported_quantity: % of expert ratings of chatbot answers scored Mika 4, 'unsatisfactory requiring substantial clarification' (incorrect or overly generalized information)
denominator: 80 reviews (10 Delphi-consensus questions answered by Perplexity AI, each rated by 8 sports-medicine fellowship-trained orthopaedic surgeons)
misinfo_definition: no definition of misinformation is given; the paper frames the task as 'to prevent the spread of misinformation, analyzing the accuracy of answers from these LLMs is essential'

reported_quantity: % of students (three countries pooled) who say they have shared some kind of disinformation
denominator: 428 first-year information-science students at 16 public universities in Brazil (196), Spain (205) and Cuba (27)
misinfo_definition: Disinformation se da cuando se comparte información falsa con el objetivo de causar daño. (Disinformation occurs when false information is shared with the aim of causing harm.)

reported_quantity: % of Albanian audience respondents who say they encountered fake news about the Russia-Ukraine war
denominator: 387 Albanian audience members who completed an online questionnaire recruited through the social media channels of Albanian public figures and online media
misinfo_definition: "dis-information as information that is false and intentionally created to harm a person, social group, organization, or state, while mis-information is indeed false information, but not created with the intent to cause harm" (Wardle & Derakhshan, 2017, as cited by the author)

reported_quantity: % of expert ratings of chatbot answers scored Mika 4, 'unsatisfactory requiring substantial clarification' (incorrect or overly generalized information)
denominator: 80 reviews (10 Delphi-consensus questions answered by ChatGPT4o, each rated by 8 sports-medicine fellowship-trained orthopaedic surgeons)
misinfo_definition: no definition of misinformation is given; the paper frames the task as 'to prevent the spread of misinformation, analyzing the accuracy of answers from these LLMs is essential'

reported_quantity: % of English Language and Literature students who reported having shared misinformation
denominator: 52 English Language and Literature students at the Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences, Osijek (of 109 valid responses); denominator includes 21 'cannot determine' answers
misinfo_definition: "Misinformation consists of false information, but the person spreading it believes to be true."

reported_quantity: % of CPR instructional videos showing failure to check for responsiveness correctly
denominator: 100 adult-CPR instructional videos retrieved with the keyword 'CPR 视频' on three Chinese short-video platforms
misinfo_definition: "Potentially inaccurate or erroneous information contained therein is highly misleading and could lead to the widespread dissemination of misinformation, with negative consequences for public health"

reported_quantity: % of expert ratings of chatbot answers scored Mika 4, 'unsatisfactory requiring substantial clarification' (incorrect or overly generalized information)
denominator: 80 reviews (10 Delphi-consensus questions answered by Claude2, each rated by 8 sports-medicine fellowship-trained orthopaedic surgeons)
misinfo_definition: no definition of misinformation is given; the paper frames the task as 'to prevent the spread of misinformation, analyzing the accuracy of answers from these LLMs is essential'

reported_quantity: % of Perplexity answers to 58 Dutch self-care questions rated 1 = inaccurate (completely incorrect and/or could lead to serious consequences)
denominator: 58 self-care questions on medicines and supplements posed in Dutch to Perplexity AI (answers scored 1-5)
misinfo_definition: 1. Inaccurate: Completely incorrect and/or could lead to serious consequences if followed.

reported_quantity: % of respondents who had seen fake news reporting word-of-mouth as a source where they observed it
denominator: 57 respondents (of the 75 Singapore-based respondents) who said they had come across fake news before (subset 'SeenFake-57')
misinfo_definition: "Fake news is news articles that are “either wholly false or containing deliberately misleading elements incorporated within its content or context" [2]."

reported_quantity: % of the Ebola tweets that were retweeted at least once which contained medical misinformation
denominator: 248 of the 564 Ebola tweets (44%) that were retweeted at least once
misinfo_definition: 'we grouped them into medically correct information, medical misinformation, and other (including tweets of a spiritual nature)'

reported_quantity: % of Bing Chat outputs that mention the Russian perspective without debunking it
denominator: Bing Chat outputs that mention the Russian perspective (a subset of its 112 outputs; Figure 3 covers N = 119 such outputs across all three chatbots)
misinfo_definition: "Russian perspective rebutted (Does the answer explicitly mention that the Russian claim is false or propagandistic?)"

reported_quantity: % of respondents who report ever having shared misinformation on social media (any topic)
denominator: 1,500 US respondents (Lightspeed Kantar online panel, quota-matched to census)
misinfo_definition: “The next questions will be about misinformation on social media. By misinformation, we mean false or misleading information.”

reported_quantity: % of survey respondents who say they receive news they believe to be false (any frequency)
denominator: 1,350 residents of the Community of Madrid aged 18-80 surveyed by 40dB (online for under-60s, telephone for older respondents); sampling error +/-2.67 points at 95% confidence
misinfo_definition: No formal definition; the paper uses 'noticias falsas' / 'desinformacion' ['fake news' / 'disinformation'] and operationalises it as respondent-perceived falsity: 'noticias que crees que son falsas' ['news that you believe is false']

reported_quantity: Mean respondent estimate of the percentage of all news that consists of misinformation, United States
denominator: 545 United States survey respondents
misinfo_definition: "we define misinformation as an overarching term to denote information that is false, inaccurate, deceptive, or not based on relevant expert knowledge"

reported_quantity: Mean respondent estimate of the % of all information encountered that is disinformation (0-100 slider)
denominator: All information the respondent encounters, as estimated by the respondent; averaged over 650 respondents in Brazil
misinfo_definition: 'Misinformation refers to false or inaccurate information in general. Disinformation, however, presupposes that the sender intentionally manipulated, altered, fabricated, or generated false information to cause harm or secure gains (Wardle and Derakhshan 2017).'

reported_quantity: % of references generated by Claude 3.5 Sonnet that were fabricated (not indexed in any database)
denominator: 480 references generated by Claude 3.5 Sonnet (4 references for each of 120 open-ended radiology questions across 8 subspecialties)
misinfo_definition: "hallucinations" defined as "fabricated or inaccurate references"; the authors state that inaccurate references "risk misinformation in clinical and academic settings"

reported_quantity: % of respondents who had seen fake news reporting instant messaging apps as a source where they observed it
denominator: 57 respondents (of the 75 Singapore-based respondents) who said they had come across fake news before (subset 'SeenFake-57')
misinfo_definition: "Fake news is news articles that are “either wholly false or containing deliberately misleading elements incorporated within its content or context" [2]."

reported_quantity: % of COVID-19 vaccine-related Reddit comments from geolocated US users that researchers manually labelled false
denominator: 5,014 manually labelled COVID-19 vaccine-related Reddit comments, drawn from 5,853 comments by users geolocated to U.S. cities/counties, themselves filtered from ~17.7 million keyword-collected Reddit comments
misinfo_definition: The World Health Organization (WHO) called this an "infodemic," which means that there is too much information, some of which is true and some of which is not, which makes it hard for people to find reliable sources and advice

reported_quantity: % of respondents who say they come across news or information that misrepresents reality or is even false every day or almost every day
denominator: French respondents in Flash Eurobarometer 464 (national n not stated; mean per-country sample 982)
misinfo_definition: "we will define fake news in this article as false or distorted information"

reported_quantity: % of ChatGPT answers to asthma questions rated as containing inaccuracies (median expert accuracy score <=3 on a 1-5 scale)
denominator: 26 ChatGPT responses (25 asthma questions plus 1 follow-up question) compiled by the authors
misinfo_definition: 'previous studies have identified a significant presence of misinformation about atopic diseases on various platforms'; accuracy operationalised by the 1-5 scale: '1, very poor/unacceptable inaccuracies; 2, poor/minor potentially harmful inaccuracies; 3, moderate/potentially misinterpretable inaccuracies; 4, good/only minor nonharmful inaccuracies; and 5, very good/no inaccuracies'

reported_quantity: % of respondents who recalled encountering the claim that nicotine is only addictive when smoked from a cigarette
denominator: 1,225 young adults aged 18-34 recruited via a Qualtrics online panel (convenience sample, oversampled for current e-cigarette users, 59.76%)
misinfo_definition: "three statements that have been promoted in either popular media or advertising for ECs", described by the authors as "misleading claims about nicotine safety"

reported_quantity: % of respondents who report never encountering false or misleading coronavirus information
denominator: 1,105 residents of Germany surveyed in Wave 3 (Respondi panel, quota-representative for age 18-69, gender and federal state)
misinfo_definition: "information on the coronavirus that you think is false or misleading"

reported_quantity: % of references generated by ChatGPT-4o with canvas that were fabricated (not indexed in any database)
denominator: 480 references generated by ChatGPT-4o with canvas (4 references for each of 120 open-ended radiology questions across 8 subspecialties)
misinfo_definition: "hallucinations" defined as "fabricated or inaccurate references"; the authors state that inaccurate references "risk misinformation in clinical and academic settings"

reported_quantity: % of Covid-19 disinformation messages classified as distortion
denominator: 802 WhatsApp messages already classified as containing Covid-19 disinformation
misinfo_definition: We understand disinformation as distorted, manipulated, or entirely false information that is created to mislead and achieve political gains

reported_quantity: % of forwarded WhatsApp messages submitted as suspected COVID-19 misinformation that the study team confirmed as COVID-19 misinformation (meeting all inclusion criteria)
denominator: 96 deduplicated WhatsApp messages forwarded to the study phone number by self-identified adult members of the South Asian diaspora (108 received)
misinfo_definition: “we use the term “misinformation” as an umbrella term to comprise false information, where the intent is not apparent”

reported_quantity: % of survey respondents who report ever recirculating information about natural remedies as protective measures against COVID-19 on social media (any frequency)
denominator: 1,249 Saudi Arabian survey respondents aged 18+ (275 health-care workers, 974 non-health-care workers) recruited via an online Google Survey link
misinfo_definition: "the sharing and resharing of medical information, whether true or false, on social media platforms regarding COVID-19"; the content of interest is "unverified claims of natural remedies" as protection against COVID-19

reported_quantity: % of commercial youth-softball-pitching websites classified as discordant with the STOP Sports Injuries guidelines
denominator: 34 commercial websites among the 86 analysed
misinfo_definition: Discordant : websites that supported behavior aligning with >=1 risk factors (eg, use of radar guns during practice to increase pitching velocity).

reported_quantity: % of respondents who reported having heard the conspiracy theory 'The COVID-19 virus is a hoax'
denominator: 895 Malawian adults aged 18+ attending outpatient, non-communicable disease or HIV clinics at 32 health facilities, recruited by systematic random sampling (every second person in the queue); AAPOR RR3 response rate 95.1%
misinfo_definition: The paper does not define misinformation formally; it operationalizes it as "ten common statements (circulating conspiracy theories in Malawi) about COVID-19 and the COVID-19 vaccine", and states "exposure to misinformation, measured here by familiarity with conspiracy theories".

reported_quantity: % of human-expert cardiology answers on the NAVER portal graded low medical accuracy by three blinded cardiologists
denominator: 237 graded human-expert answers (out of 251 cardiology question-answer pairs collected from NAVER; the paper does not explain the 237 vs 251 gap)
misinfo_definition: "Accurate medical advice is paramount in ensuring optimal patient care, and misinformation can lead to misguided decisions with potentially detrimental health outcomes."

reported_quantity: % of respondents who say they come across news or information that misrepresents reality or is even false every day or almost every day
denominator: 24,551 respondents aged 15+ across 25 EU countries (Flash Eurobarometer 464, mean per country 982, min 505 Luxembourg, max 1,015 Great Britain)
misinfo_definition: "we will define fake news in this article as false or distorted information"
